Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

dynasimR 0.2.0

Plots and reproducibility

  • plot_radar() now joins the metrics of a scenario with straight lines on evenly spaced spokes. Before, the outline was bent into spirals and the metric names were clipped. Metric names are written outside the rim, ring values replace the overlapping radial axis, and the new argument rescale (default FALSE) puts metrics with different units on a common 0-1 axis.
  • plot_scenario_heatmap() and the tile variant of plot_sdi_map() choose a light or dark label colour per tile; values on dark tiles and region names on near-white tiles were unreadable.
  • plot_sdi_map() uses a red-blue instead of a red-green diverging scale, so under- and oversupply stay distinguishable with colour-vision deficiency, and reports a missing region or sdi_median column by name.
  • plot_al_tradeoff() draws the AL labels above the optimum ring in a neutral colour, keeps the threshold label inside the panel, and says so when no autonomy level meets the threshold instead of printing a missing optimum.
  • plot_km() and the policy narrative print p-values with their relation (“p = 0.005”, “p < 0.001”). With one stratifying variable the legend and the risk table show the levels only, with the variable as legend title.
  • plot_cost_effectiveness() places scenario labels above their points and inside the panel; it, plot_map(color_by = "status") and plot_timeline() use the package palette and titled legends. plot_timeline() explains its line and band in the caption.
  • policy_effect(), al_efficiency(), compute_compliance_index(), compute_wait_gap_index() and group_effect() gain a seed argument (default NULL, the previous behaviour). A supplied seed makes the bootstrap intervals reproducible and leaves the caller’s random-number state unchanged. The vignettes and examples now set it.
  • print() for policy_effect() results wraps the narrative to the console width instead of printing one long line.
  • Dashboard: static plots are rendered at 96 pixels per inch, so their text matches the size of the surrounding interface; effect-size, test and trade-off tables show four significant digits (sorting and export keep full precision); the autonomy tab names the scenarios of the default sweep that a dataset lacks, and its legend no longer overlaps the axis title. Its trade-off plot keeps the shaded compliant band and the threshold label, which the conversion to an interactive plot used to drop.
  • The examples of al_efficiency() and plot_al_tradeoff() map the two autonomy levels of the bundled data instead of the full default sweep, which produced a single-point plot.
  • plot_al_tradeoff() labels autonomy levels below the compliance threshold underneath their point, so the label no longer sits on the threshold line. print() for al_efficiency() results names the mapped scenarios that are missing from the data.
  • plot_al_tradeoff() draws its interval whiskers opaque enough to see, stops the palette before the pale yellow that vanished on white, and states in the caption that the whiskers are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals.
  • The tile variant of plot_sdi_map() picks white or near-black region names from the luminance of each tile, so mid-red tiles no longer carry white text with too little contrast.
  • plot_policy() titles its group axis and states in a caption that points are differences of medians and whiskers percentile bootstrap intervals at the chosen level. plot_progress_curves() explains its bars, whiskers, lines and bands in a caption and titles its legend.
  • plot_map() titles its legend (“Group” or “Status”), and plot_scenario_heatmap() and plot_sdi_map() draw a wider colour bar so that their break labels no longer run together. The innermost ring of plot_radar() is no longer labelled, where the outlines covered it.
  • The vignette figures carry alternative text.

CRAN preparation

  • Every exported function now has a runnable example. Examples write only to temporary files, and the dashboard example runs only in interactive sessions.
  • Expand the Description field, declare the maintainer ORCID and rewrite cran-comments.md.
  • The documentation uses British English spelling throughout.
  • CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json name the author as R. Heller.
  • read_simulation() reads simulation files smaller than 8 MiB on one thread. readr otherwise starts a thread per core for every file, which took longer than reading the bundled example files themselves.
  • fill_placeholders() no longer computes bootstrap intervals for the compliance index, of which it substitutes only the point estimate. The substituted values are unchanged, and the function runs about twice as fast.
  • The README no longer links to the maintenance notes, which are not part of the package source.

Changes since 0.1.0 (prepared as 0.1.1, never released)

  • Verify staged figure output before reporting success or replacing an existing file. Preserve prior exports on device failure, and enable the shared macOS XQuartz setup for SVG checks. Refuse failed SVG initialisation before drawing on the caller’s device or opening a default output file.
  • Validate each input file and preserve caller-supplied scenario metadata. Report zero-demand ratios as undefined, correct stage completion counts, and distinguish descriptive percentiles from confidence intervals.
  • Correct signed policy narratives, bootstrap intervals and pooled effect sizes; reject invalid survival observations and missing model predictors.
  • Preserve source manuscripts and existing outputs, treat identifiers as literal data, and validate requested placeholders before writing.
  • Repair dashboard selection and profile handling, literal-text rendering, figure formats and LaTeX table compilation.
  • Add actual survival risk tables, current ggplot2 interval geometry, portable developer checks and reproducible regression coverage.
  • Clarify development/publication status; no new release has been published.

dynasimR 0.1.0

  • Standardize the named v5 package logo across README, documentation pages and available application headers, with matching light and dark artwork.

Initial release.

Features

  • Load and validate simulation outputs for two interchangeable profiles via read_simulation() / load_example_data().
  • Time-to-event analysis with km_estimate(), cox_model(), plot_km(), plot_forest().
  • Policy-effect quantification via policy_effect() with auto-generated LaTeX-ready narrative.
  • Autonomy-level trade-off analysis via al_efficiency() and plot_al_tradeoff().
  • Compliance Index via compute_compliance_index() with bootstrap confidence intervals.
  • Profile B helpers: progress_trajectory(), compute_wait_gap_index(), group_effect(), spatial_supply_demand(), compute_completion_analysis().
  • Manuscript export: export_figure(), export_latex_table(), fill_placeholders() (publisher-template compatible).
  • Embedded Shiny dashboard via launch_app().
  • Example data shipped for reproducible demos and tests.
